                    ### Question
                    Which of the following cytokines exert an anti-inflammatory and immunosuppressive effect?

                    ### Options
                    opa. Interleukin-1 alpha, interleukin-1 beta.
opb. Tumor necrosis factor-alpha, Tumor necrosis factor-beta.
opc. Interleukin-17, Interleukin-22.
opd. Interleukin-10, Transforming growth factor beta.
ope. Interleukin 2, Interferon-gamma.

### Enhanced Information (For Contextual Support):
Interleukin-10 and Transforming Growth Factor beta are well-established anti-inflammatory and immunosuppressive cytokines. Interleukin-10 inhibits pro-inflammatory cytokines, leading to reduced inflammation and an overall immunosuppressive effect. Transforming Growth Factor beta suppresses immune cell activation, contributing to a decreased inflammatory response. In contrast, Interleukin-1 alpha, Interleukin-1 beta, Tumor necrosis factor-alpha, Tumor necrosis factor-beta, Interleukin-17, Interleukin-22, Interleukin-2, and Interferon-gamma are all pro-inflammatory cytokines that promote inflammation and do not exert anti-inflammatory effects. Therefore, the correct answer is option (opd): Interleukin-10 and Transforming Growth Factor beta.
